messages:
susan: Hey team — customer on acct acme-corp reporting intermittent 502s + TLS handshake failures when calling our API over their TGW+VPN -> hits our Interface VPC Endpoint. Seen since ~08:15 UTC.

raj: Ack. Any quick repro from their side? curl / dig / openssl output would help.

susan: They ran this from on‑prem jump: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/health --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:10.0.5.23` -> TLS handshake failure: "sslv3 alert handshake failure". `dig +short api.redwood.ai` -> `10.0.5.23` (interface ENI).

maria: Two quick checks: 1) Are they resolving to the interface ENI IP via Route53 PHZ/forwarder? 2) Is there TLS inspection on the egress path that could rewrite SNI?

chris: Also verify TGW route to the ENI subnets, and that ENIs don't have src/dst checks (should be disabled for interface endpoints). Can they run: 
```
traceroute 10.0.5.23
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.23:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -msg
```

susan: They shared outputs: traceroute goes TGW -> transit -> VPC -> ENI. `openssl s_client` shows ClientHello then an immediate TLS alert. Customer suspects a Palo Alto TLS‑inspect box in their egress.

raj: If the firewall terminates and re‑establishes TLS, SNI/header can be replaced with the firewall cert/hostname. Our ALB/host routing expects SNI/Host `api.redwood.ai` to hit the right target — if that's changed the backend will 502 or reject.

support-bot: pulled backend logs around reported times -> 2x 502s from src 10.0.5.23; Host header observed: `api.redwood.internal` (does not match public hostname).

maria: Confirms likely TLS MITM. Recommended remediation: bypass TLS inspection for destination ENI CIDRs, or configure the FW to preserve SNI/pass-through for traffic to our endpoints.

chris: Practical runbook for customer:
1) `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=description,Values=*vpce*` to list ENI IPs/CIDRs.
2) Add those CIDRs to firewall egress bypass (no TLS inspect).
3) Test: `openssl s_client -connect <eni_ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.ai` -> verify cert CN/SAN is `api.redwood.ai`.
4) Re-run `curl` against real hostname (no `--resolve`).

raj: Short term workaround if they cannot change FW: route traffic out via a nat/proxy that preserves SNI (but customer ops may not want this). Longer term: consider dedicated public peering or a PrivateConnect arrangement (needs sales/infra).

susan: Customer applied bypass for the ENI range and retested — they report calls are now succeeding. They said: "bypass for privatelink ENIs fixed it".

maria: Good. Add note to customer case: document which firewall rule to change + ENI IPs so future rotations are handled (ENIs can change on endpoint updates). Recommend they maintain Route53 resolver + PHZ association if using conditional forwarders.

susan: Closing here, will attach evidence and update ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:
